messages:
Alex J: FYI — customer hit a bunch of 400s and a billing spike when calling /embeddings. They send a single item sometimes and a list other times. Error: \"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1\". Any quick theories?
Maria S: Ugh that screams client-side shape issue. Are they sending a stringified JSON or NDJSON/gzip?
Alex J: They said using node-fetch + gzip to pack many requests. Example payload they pasted:
```json
{\"input\": \"\\\"some text\\\"\"}
```
Sam Dev: That payload is double-encoded — input becomes a single string that contains JSON. On batch path we expect an array like `[\"text1\",\"text2\"]` not `\"[\\\"text\\\"]\"`.
Ingrid L: Did we see this as a unique customer mistake before? I recall a similar support case but client used axios + qs that flattened arrays.
Alex J: I repro'd quickly: curl with Content-Type: application/json + body `{\"input\":\"foo\"}` returns 400 and logs show: `BadRequest: embedding vector length 1 != model.dim(1536)`.
Maria S: Can we suggest exact repro and a one-line fix? Customer asks for a patch they can drop into code.
Sam Dev: Sure — two quick fixes depending on client:
1) If they mean single-item batch, wrap in array: `{\"input\": [\"foo\"]}`
2) If using gzip/ndjson, ensure Content-Type set to `application/x-ndjson` and each line is a JSON array or object per our spec.
Alex J: Shared a tiny node snippet that caused the issue:
```js
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer x', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ input: JSON.stringify([text]) }) // <- oops double stringify
})
```
Ingrid L: Nice catch. Also check for some clients that auto-serialize arrays into querystring-like `input[]=a&input[]=b` which becomes a different shape when converted to JSON on the server.
Maria S: For the reply to customer, let's be explicit. Suggested reply: `Please ensure the JSON body uses an array for batch inputs (e.g. {\"input\": [\"a\",\"b\"]}) and avoid double-encoding strings. If you gzip/NDJSON your payload set Content-Type accordingly. If you paste the exact request body we can verify.` Sound good?
Alex J: I'll send that. Also added a small repro test to support-runbook: a curl matrix showing the bad vs good payloads.
Sam Dev: Can you paste the curl examples here so support copy/pastes are clean?
Alex J: Yep — two quick curl repros:
Bad:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"input\":\"\\\"hello\\\"\"}'
```
Good (single item batch):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"input\":[\"hello\"]}'
```
Good (ndjson, many items):
```
echo -e '{\"input\":[\"a\"]}\n{\"input\":[\"b\"]}' | gzip | curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/x-ndjson\" \
  --data-binary @- --compressed
```
Maria S: Perfect. Add a note to include model name in error reports — sometimes dimension differs across models (e.g., text-embedding-1536 vs 768).
Alex J: Good call. I added that.
SupportBot: Incident note attached: case #C-78924 — root cause: client double-serialized input causing shape mismatch -> 400 -> retries -> billing spike.
Ingrid L: Can we also update our docs snippet to show both singleton and batch examples in the same section? I can PR.
Sam Dev: I'll add a lint rule in examples to block JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(...)) in our JS examples :sweat_smile:
Alex J: Thanks all. Customer replied they patched and errors stopped. Marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
